correctness.rationale: For G=A⋊C2 inversion, a normal N≤A has quotient Dih(A/N). If N meets the reflection coset, then H=N∩A contains 2A, N=H ∪ H(as) for a coset a+H and G/N=A/H elementary 2-group. Nontrivial elementary 2-quotients also arise as Dih(B), B=(C2)^(r-1)≤A, so every nontrivial type is Dih(B). Dih(B) embeds Dih(C) iff B embeds C, using the subgroup generated by elements of order>2 or 2-rank bound in exponent-2 case. Finite abelian subgroup types form componentwise bounded partition distributive lattices, with one extra bottom trivial quotient. For d=rank(A/2A), normal kernels of (C2)^r split into [d r-1]_2 inside A and 2^r[d r]_2 outside. Independent multiplication-table subgroup/normal enumeration verified 7 finite groups incl A=C4×C2. Exact rank-0 and A=0 boundaries checked.

originality.rationale: Halder–Ballal (Oct 2026) already treat QIso for abelian G, cyclic dihedral groups and describe generalized-dihedral normal quotients (Lemma 3.1), so these pieces are strictly prior. Their generalized-dihedral lemma gives only reflection coset Ht, whereas distinct H(as) produce a nontrivial 2^r kernel multiplicity. The full noncyclic-inversion-kernel quotient-type lattice, embedding rigidity, and exact multiplicity fiber are not stated or implied by their cyclic lattice theorem, as actually read. Novelty PASS qualified by older finite group subgroup-type literature.
residual_risks: An older structural theorem about quotient-self-dual groups or isomorphism-type lattices may implicitly yield the noncyclic lattice; no claim of exhaustive historical uniqueness.
The published Lemma 3.1 formula N=H∪Ht for arbitrary nonrotation normal kernels is too restrictive; exact coset-twisted count matters and is independently rederived.

value.rationale: Classifying the entire quotient-type lattice of generalized dihedral groups with arbitrary finite abelian kernels extends a natural cyclic classification to noncyclic p-primary variation; elementary 2-rank quotient fiber multiplicities show how a single type can correspond to many normal kernels. It resolves a motivated exact group-lattice/enumerative question rather than merely renaming cyclic formulas.
